methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective real-world study leverages the large Flatiron Health EHR-derived database with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria aligned to monarchE cohort 1. Two distinct analyses are performed with appropriate comparator groups (high-risk vs non-high-risk vs eTNBC context). Multivariable logistic regression (utilization) and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models (outcomes) adjust for plausibly relevant confounders, and sensitivity analyses using initial diagnosis as time zero are included. Limitations (Ki-67 missingness >50%, unmeasured comorbidities/financial barriers, immortal time/time-origin differences between cohorts) are acknowledged. Kaplan-Meier with hazard ratios and 95% CIs are reported; no formal power calculation is described and no multiplicity correction is mentioned across the many subgroup comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study directly informs adjuvant treatment decisions by quantifying a guideline-care gap (60% of eligible patients not receiving abemaciclib) and by characterizing real-world recurrence/mortality in monarchE-eligible patients treated with ET alone. Findings that N+ high-risk outcomes approximate eTNBC outcomes have direct implications for patient counseling and treatment intensification. Design is an individual retrospective cohort study drawn from a multi-institution US EHR database, corresponding to Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational cohort analysis of EHR data, STROBE is the applicable standard. Most STROBE elements are addressed: study design, setting, eligibility criteria, variables, statistical methods, participant flow with attrition supplementary figures, baseline characteristics, and limitations. The manuscript does not explicitly reference STROBE or provide a checklist, and some STROBE items (e.g., handling of missing data beyond Ki-67, explicit treatment of loss to follow-up) are only partially addressed. Flatiron Health data are proprietary and accessible only under license; no code sharing statement is evident, so reproducibility is limited.

novelty_literature.justification: Real-world abemaciclib utilization has been reported previously (cited single-institution studies showing <50% uptake), and prior real-world recurrence analyses in this population exist (Sheffield et al. 2022 is cited). The present work's contribution is a larger, multi-institution contemporary dataset and the explicit benchmarking of N+ high-risk outcomes against eTNBC, together with nodal-subgroup risk stratification within the FDA-approved monarchE cohort 1 population. This is a meaningful extension rather than a first-in-class finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear introduction framing the monarchE evidence base, transparent methods split into two studies, and a discussion that maps findings to clinical implications. Key numerical results (e.g., 5-year IDFS 70.9% vs 91.2%; HRs >=2.3) are foregrounded. Tables and figures are referenced systematically though several appear primarily in supplementary material. Minor redundancy exists between abstract highlights and conclusions.

key_strengths: Large contemporary multi-institution Flatiron Health cohort (n=3170 for utilization; n=6350 for outcomes) with 56-month median follow-up supporting stable 5-year estimates
Clinically actionable quantification of the treatment gap (60% non-utilization) and risk stratification within FDA-approved monarchE cohort 1 eligibility
Novel benchmarking showing N+ high-risk HR+/HER2- outcomes approximate eTNBC outcomes, directly motivating treatment intensification
Appropriate multivariable adjustment (Cox and logistic regression) and pre-specified sensitivity analyses using initial diagnosis as time origin
key_concerns: Ki-67 missing for >50% of patients, risking misclassification of non-high-risk group and biasing relative risk estimates (acknowledged)
Unmeasured confounders (comorbidities, patient preference, financial toxicity) not captured in EHR data limit causal interpretation of utilization gaps
Time-origin differences between HR+/HER2- cohorts (adjuvant ET initiation) and eTNBC cohort (adjuvant chemotherapy initiation) complicate direct outcome comparison despite sensitivity analysis
No explicit STROBE checklist, no multiplicity correction for the many subgroup comparisons, and proprietary Flatiron data limit reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid observational real-world evidence with clear clinical messaging and methodologically adequate execution, but incremental novelty and observational design cap the ceiling at a strong Tier 2 oncology journal (e.g., ESMO Open / JCO PO range) rather than a top practice-changing Tier 1 venue.
